addons.help_body:
ADDON NAMING INSTRUCTIONS

So the smart engine can protect your WIM image from mismatches, files must include their architecture in the filename BEFORE the extension.

Correct Examples:
  >  MyLanguagePack_x64_en-us.tpk
  >  Tool_arm64_main.tpk
  >  Tool_main.bpk

Why does this matter?
If you add an entire folder of Addons, the script reads these suffixes and automatically SKIPS packages/Registry files targeting a different architecture (x86, x64, or ARM64), preventing BSODs and image corruption.

DeltaPack Dual-Engine Packages:
Select the 'manifest_*.json' file inside the package folder to add it as a single unit (WIM + REG + Removals + Actions, in the order defined by the manifest).

desc.Fax: Allows sending and receiving faxes. Unnecessary if you do not use a fax modem.
desc.PrintSpooler: Manages print jobs. Disable only if you do not use any printer (physical or virtual such as PDF).
desc.RemoteRegistry: Allows remote users to modify the Registry. Recommended to disable for security.
desc.SysMain: Maintains and improves system performance (formerly Superfetch). May cause high disk usage on HDDs.
desc.TabletInputService: Enables the touch keyboard and handwriting panel. Unnecessary on desktop PCs without touchscreens.
desc.WalletService: System service for Windows Wallet. Unnecessary if unused.
desc.wisvc: Manages participation in the Windows Insider Program. Unnecessary if not using preview builds.
desc.AJRouter: Related to AllJoyn IoT (Internet of Things) device communication. Unnecessary for most users.
desc.MapsBroker: For the 'Windows Maps' app. Unnecessary if you use other map services (Google/Waze).
desc.icssvc: Allows sharing an internet connection with other devices (Mobile Hotspot). Unnecessary if unused.
desc.WSearch: Provides content indexing and search results for files, email, and other content.
desc.fhsvc: File History service. Unnecessary if you use other backup software or do not use File History.
desc.TrkWks: Maintains shortcuts to files moved across NTFS volumes. Low impact, safe to disable.
desc.RetailDemo: Runs an OS demo for retail store display PCs. Useless for end users.
desc.DPS: Diagnostic Policy Service. If you do not use built-in Windows troubleshooters, you can disable it to save resources.
desc.WdiServiceHost: Diagnostic Service Host. Together with DPS, handles error diagnostics and troubleshooting. Safe to disable for performance.
desc.WdiSystemHost: Diagnostic System Host. Companion to WdiServiceHost. Disabling it reduces background diagnostic activity.
desc.PcaSvc: Program Compatibility Assistant. Monitors installations and shows prompts like 'Did this program install correctly?'. Safe to disable.
desc.FontCache: Optimizes performance by caching fonts. Disabling saves RAM but may slightly slow initial font loading.
desc.FontCache3_0_0_0: Legacy Windows Presentation Foundation (WPF) font cache service. Generally safe to disable.
desc.TermService: Allows users to connect remotely to this PC using Remote Desktop.
desc.WMPNetworkSvc: Shares Windows Media Player libraries with other networked devices.
desc.DiagTrack: Primary telemetry service (Connected User Experiences and Telemetry). Disabling it improves privacy.
desc.lfsvc: Allows apps to access GPS and network location. Disable for privacy if unused.
desc.CscService: Offline Files service for accessing network files offline. Unnecessary for home users.
desc.StiSvc: Windows Image Acquisition (WIA) service. Required for scanners and older cameras.
desc.SSDPSRV: Discovers devices on the local network (media servers, printers). Unnecessary if not sharing media.
desc.upnphost: Allows hosting UPnP devices on the network. Similar to SSDPSRV, unnecessary if not sharing on LAN.
desc.WbioSrvc: Windows Biometric Service. Can be disabled if you do not use fingerprint or facial recognition (Windows Hello).
desc.WerSvc: Windows Error Reporting service. Sends crash data to Microsoft when an app fails. Safe to disable.
desc.GraphicsPerfSvc: Monitors graphics performance. Rarely needed unless using specific GPU diagnostic tools.
desc.Wecsvc: Windows Event Collector. Gathers events from other PCs on the network. Unnecessary for home users.
desc.iphlpsvc: IP Helper. Provides IPv6 tunnel connectivity (6to4, ISATAP, Teredo). Unnecessary for most home IPv4 users.
desc.lmhosts: TCP/IP NetBIOS Helper. Legacy network protocol for file sharing. Unnecessary on modern networks using direct SMB.
desc.TapiSrv: Telephony. Provides TAPI support for legacy apps, modems, and fax. Obsolete for most modern users.
desc.WPDBusEnum: Portable Device Enumerator Service. Syncs content with older MP3 players/phones in Windows Media Player. Rarely needed today.
desc.MixedRealityOpenXRSvc: Windows Mixed Reality OpenXR Service. Enables VR/MR headset features. Unnecessary without VR/AR hardware.
desc.spectrum: Windows Perception Service. Manages spatial perception for VR/AR (HoloLens). Unnecessary for standard desktop use.
desc.Netlogon: Maintains a secure channel between this PC and a domain controller. Unnecessary on home PCs not joined to an enterprise domain.
desc.XblAuthManager: Xbox Live Auth Manager. Disable if you do not use Microsoft Store games or Xbox Game Bar.
desc.XblGameSave: Xbox Live Game Save cloud sync service. Unnecessary if unused.
desc.XboxGipSvc: Xbox Accessory Management Service. Unnecessary if no Xbox peripherals are connected to the PC.
desc.XboxNetApiSvc: Xbox Live Networking Service. Disable if you do not use Xbox online features.
desc.WpcMonSvc: Parental Controls service. Unnecessary if you do not manage child accounts on this PC.
desc.PhoneSvc: Phone Service. Manages telephony state on the device, typically linked to the 'Phone Link' app. Disable if unused.

desc.t01: Prevents Windows from automatically downloading Candy Crush, Spotify, and other sponsored apps when connected to the internet.
desc.t02: Prevents Windows from showing 'Welcome' tips and suggestions that often install unwanted software.
desc.t03: Allocates 100% of CPU to games and multimedia, removing the 20% reservation for background tasks.
desc.t04: Forces the multimedia scheduler to assign maximum GPU priority to fullscreen applications.
desc.t05: Forces the multimedia scheduler to assign high CPU priority to games.
desc.t06: Disables Xbox Game DVR at machine policy level to prevent FPS stutters.
desc.t07: Hardware-Accelerated GPU Scheduling. Reduces gaming latency (requires compatible hardware).
desc.t08: Adjusts the scheduler to give higher CPU priority to the active foreground window.
desc.t09: Increases the filesystem cache. Recommended for systems with more than 8GB of RAM.
desc.t10: Reduces the timeout before stopping services during shutdown (2000ms).
desc.t11: Prevents Windows from indexing the entire drive, limiting indexing to libraries and desktop to save CPU/disk.
desc.t12: Recommended for SSDs. Avoids constant memory preloading and reduces write wear.
desc.t13: Frees gigabytes of space on drive C: by disabling the Windows hibernation file.
desc.t14: Improves gaming performance (up to 15%) by turning off virtualization-based security. (Reduces security).
desc.t15: Turns off the offline maps manager. Great for saving RAM if you do not use Windows Maps.
desc.t16: WARNING: Enable this ONLY if you will never use a physical printer or Print to PDF. Saves RAM and reduces attack surface.
desc.t17: Removes the artificial delay when launching startup programs at machine level.
desc.t18: Prevents desktop and Explorer icons from reloading or flickering.
desc.t19: Removes the AI assistant from the taskbar via machine policy.
desc.t20: Removes animated illustrations from the search box at machine level.
desc.t21: Removes the virtual desktops icon from the taskbar for all users.
desc.t22: Displays a crisp login background without the GPU-intensive acrylic blur effect.
desc.t23: Blocks tracking for personalized ads at machine level.
desc.t24: Reduces data sent to Microsoft to the minimum level (Security Only).
desc.t25: Prevents AI from capturing periodic snapshots of your activity.
desc.t27: Prevents what you type in the Start Menu from being sent to the internet.
desc.t28: Prevents Store apps from running in the background for all users.
desc.t29: Prevents Windows from sending crash and app failure reports to Microsoft servers.
desc.t30: Prevents Windows from tracking which programs you open to personalize the Start Menu.
desc.t31: Turns off the 'Connected User Experiences and Telemetry' service at kernel level.
desc.t32: Turns off the push message routing service used by Microsoft for telemetry collection.
desc.t33: Disables system problem diagnostics, reducing background disk and CPU usage.
desc.t34: Disables multimedia network throttling to free up connection bandwidth.
desc.t35: Disables the Network Data Usage monitor, which frequently causes non-paged pool memory leaks.
desc.t36: Removes 'Show more options' and displays the full classic right-click menu machine-wide.
desc.t37: Lets you read the stop code on a Blue Screen of Death without the PC immediately rebooting.
desc.t38: Allows Windows to handle file paths exceeding the classic 260-character limit system-wide.
desc.t39: Hides toast popups and completely disables the Notification Center for all users.

editions.Core: Microsoft's standard consumer edition. Designed for most home users with all core features, lower cost, and without unnecessary enterprise modules. Great for gaming and everyday home tasks.
editions.CoreN: Basic edition designed for the European market ('N' regulation). Includes all standard Home features without preinstalled media technologies such as Windows Media Player, Skype, or Voice Recorder.
editions.CoreK: Editions designed for the South Korean market ('K/KN' regulation). Includes links to third-party media and messaging software to comply with Korean antitrust regulations.
editions.CoreSingleLanguage: Designed for home users and budget OEM devices. Supports only a single base display language, ideal for users who want a simplified setup without switching system languages.
editions.CoreCountrySpecific: Geographically restricted edition typically distributed in specific emerging markets (such as China). Functionally identical to Home, but locked to a specific region.
editions.Professional: Advanced Microsoft edition designed for professionals, businesses, and organizations. Includes BitLocker, Hyper-V, Remote Desktop, and domain join capabilities.
editions.ProfessionalN: Professional edition for the European market. Includes all Windows Pro security and management features (Hyper-V, BitLocker) without preinstalled media applications.
editions.ProfessionalSingleLanguage: Variant of Windows Pro commonly licensed to OEMs, restricted to a single display language while retaining full business capabilities.
editions.ProfessionalCountrySpecific: Variant of Windows Pro restricted to a specific country or region for licensing purposes.
editions.ProfessionalWorkstation: Designed for high-performance workloads such as data science, 3D rendering, and CAD. Supports server-grade hardware (Xeon/EPYC CPUs, up to 6TB RAM) and Resilient File System (ReFS).
editions.ProfessionalWorkstationN: High-performance Workstation edition for the European market. Full server-grade hardware and ReFS support without preinstalled media components.
editions.ProfessionalEducation: Variant of Windows Pro built on the same architecture with education-focused defaults, removing Cortana tips and ads to minimize classroom distractions.
editions.ProfessionalEducationN: European education variant of Windows Pro with classroom defaults, no ads, and no preinstalled media software.
editions.Enterprise: Part of Microsoft 365 Enterprise. Provides advanced device management, deep telemetry controls, and enterprise security features like Credential Guard for large organizations.
editions.EnterpriseN: Corporate edition for the European market. Offers the same advanced management and reduced telemetry as standard Enterprise without bundled media players or codecs.
editions.EnterpriseS: Designed for mission-critical environments requiring maximum stability (Long-Term Servicing Channel). Offers long-term support, quality-only updates, and omits Cortana, Edge, and the Microsoft Store.
editions.EnterpriseSN: The cleanest, most stable edition for Europe. Long-Term Servicing Channel (LTSC) without Microsoft Store, Cortana, Edge, or preinstalled media components.
editions.EnterpriseG: Specialized government edition originally created under strict security and data sovereignty requirements for the Chinese government (Zhuangongban), with heavily restricted telemetry and custom encryption.
editions.EnterpriseGN: Specialized government edition variant without preinstalled media components.
editions.ServerRdsh: Unique edition designed specifically for Azure Virtual Desktop. Allows multiple interactive users to sign in simultaneously to the same VM, combining client experience with server scalability.
editions.Education: Built for academic institutions on top of Windows Enterprise. Delivers enterprise-grade security and management licensed and tailored for students, teachers, and school staff.
editions.EducationN: Enterprise-based edition for European schools. Includes full academic security and management without Microsoft's native media ecosystem.
editions.Cloud: Edition tailored for education or low-end devices. Highly secure and locked down, allowing only Microsoft Store apps and Microsoft Edge.
editions.CloudN: European variant of Windows 10 S without native media capabilities.
editions.CloudEdition: Highly streamlined and restricted edition optimized for classroom performance and security on low-cost K-8 education devices prioritizing web apps.
editions.CloudEditionN: European variant of Windows 11 SE without Windows Media Player or bundled media add-ons.
editions.IoTEnterprise: Full enterprise edition engineered for embedded systems, kiosks, ATMs, and point-of-sale (POS) terminals. Includes specialized lockdown features (Assigned Access / Kiosk Mode).
editions.IoTEnterpriseK: Windows IoT Enterprise edition for the South Korean market, complying with antitrust rules by omitting default media software while targeting ATMs and embedded systems.
editions.IoTEnterpriseS: The definitive edition for mission-critical hardware (medical devices, industrial machinery, ATMs). Combines IoT kiosk lockdowns with 10 years of support and LTSC stability.
editions.IoTEnterpriseSK: Long-Term Servicing Channel (LTSC) IoT variant designed specifically for the South Korean market without media components.
editions.ServerStandard: Windows Server edition with Desktop Experience (GUI). Designed for physical or lightly virtualized environments, ideal for small and medium businesses.
editions.ServerStandardCore: Windows Server Standard installed in Server Core mode (no GUI). Greatly reduces attack surface and resource footprint for remote administration and infrastructure roles.
editions.ServerDatacenter: Premium Windows Server edition with Desktop Experience. Built for highly virtualized datacenters and software-defined cloud environments, including Storage Spaces Direct and Shielded VMs.
editions.ServerDatacenterCore: Windows Server Datacenter in Server Core mode. Maximum security and efficiency for large-scale hypervisors and software-defined datacenters without GUI overhead.
editions.ServerAzureCor: Exclusive edition for Azure cloud and Azure Stack HCI. Supports Hotpatching (installing security updates without rebooting) and SMB over QUIC.
editions.ServerTurbine: Desktop Experience edition exclusive to Azure and Azure Local (Azure Stack HCI), supporting SMB over QUIC and advanced virtual networking.
editions.ServerTurbineCor: Server Core variant of Windows Server Datacenter: Azure Edition optimized for cloud workloads and Hotpatching.
editions.ServerStandardACor: Annual Channel / ACor release of Windows Server Standard in Server Core mode.
editions.ServerDatacenterACor: Annual Channel / ACor release of Windows Server Datacenter in Server Core mode.
editions.ServerStandardEval: Evaluation edition of Windows Server Standard with Desktop Experience (180 days).
editions.ServerStandardCoreEval: Evaluation edition of Windows Server Standard in Server Core mode (180 days).
editions.ServerDatacenterEval: Evaluation edition of Windows Server Datacenter with Desktop Experience (180 days).
editions.ServerDatacenterCoreEval: Evaluation edition of Windows Server Datacenter in Server Core mode (180 days).
editions.ServerSolution: Edition tailored for small businesses with up to 25 users and 50 devices.
editions.EnterpriseEval: Corporate evaluation edition of Windows Enterprise (90 days) for compatibility testing and enterprise deployment.
editions.EnterpriseNEval: Evaluation edition of Windows Enterprise N for the European market (without preinstalled media technologies).
editions.EnterpriseSEval: Evaluation edition of Windows Enterprise Long-Term Servicing Channel (LTSC).
editions.EnterpriseSNEval: European evaluation edition of Windows Enterprise LTSC N without media components.
editions.IoTEnterpriseSEval: Evaluation edition of Windows IoT Enterprise LTSC for validating embedded and industrial devices.
editions.PPIPro: Specialized Windows edition built for Surface Hub collaborative devices and meeting rooms.
editions.WNC: Edition optimized for Windows 365 / Cloud PC cloud desktop environments.
editions.Starter: Entry-level basic edition with minimal system requirements.
editions.StarterN: Entry-level basic edition for the European market without preinstalled media components.
